about: Numbers the Simulation, Map and UI roles can cite. 'verify': true = still a working assumption; do not present as fact. Entries without a verify flag are cited in their source field.

jezeroMeasured.source: Computed from public/data/weather.json and dust.json (Perseverance MEDA + Mastcam-Z, 118 sols sampled across ~2.6 Mars years)

windMS.note: Wind data only up to sol 313 (sensor damaged)

surfaceAlbedo.source: Perseverance MEDA broadband albedo (0.3-3 um): Martinez et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007537 (traverse mean 0.12 +/- 0.01 as cited by Munguira et al. 2023, JGR Planets, e2022JE007559); noon range and TES value from Martinez et al., LPSC 2022 abstract 2024. Used as the albedo in sunlight.json.

thermalInertia.source: Perseverance MEDA, Martinez et al. 2023, JGR Planets 128, e2022JE007537 (abstract)

solSeconds.source: MEDA PDS readme (24 h 39 min 35.244 s)

lightTimeOneWayMin.source: Checked in proposal §9 (Nov 14): about 3-22 minutes one way

o2KgPerDay.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document, NASA/TP-2015-218570/REV2 (Feb 2022, NTRS 20210024855), Table 3-23 (HIDH reference crewmember, short mission): 0.84 kg O2 consumed and 1.01 kg CO2 produced per day

co2KgPerDay.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document, NASA/TP-2015-218570/REV2 (Feb 2022, NTRS 20210024855), Table 3-23: 1.01 kg CO2 per day (rounded to 1.0)

waterLPerDay.source: NASA Life Support Baseline Values and Assumptions Document, NASA/TP-2015-218570/REV2 (Feb 2022, NTRS 20210024855), Table 3-31 and section 3.3.5 (p. 73), and Table 4-20: 2.00 kg/crewmember-day drinking water (from NASA HIDH 2014, assumed for all future missions) plus 0.5 kg for food preparation = 2.5 kg potable water

perseveranceMmrtgW.note: at mission start, declining a few % per year

moxieO2GramsPerHour.source: NASA: rated 300 W for 6-12 g/h, checked in proposal §9

perseveranceRadio.uhf: about 400 MHz, up to 2 Mbit/s to relay orbiters (MRO, Odyssey, ESA's TGO and Mars Express), relayed to the Deep Space Network. MAVEN was lost in 2025.
perseveranceRadio.xBandHighGain: direct to Earth, mostly for receiving commands
perseveranceRadio.source: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 landing press kit, Telecommunications; current orbiters from the Mars Relay Network Handbook, JPL D-71874 Release 4 (April 2026). Pass times: relay.json

softSandThermalInertia.source: Design threshold backed by measurements: Jezero sand dune 180 (MEDA, Martinez et al. 2023); Gale's active Bagnold dunes 200-310, mean 240 +/- 20 from THEMIS (Edwards et al. 2018, JGR Planets, doi:10.1029/2017JE005501); loose particulate material is below ~350 (same paper). Below 200 picks the finest, loosest material; THEMIS pixels are 100 m, so cells mix sand and rock.
